prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Sentinel Vale: land/coastal/cryosphere products; predictable latency/documented quality; ground excludes spacecraft/launch/external processing except interfaces. Mission Control Center (Bluebell): supervision/planning/authorized-command release; receives prepass antenna/link/timing/routing-readiness→Network Control System (Lantern), authoritative circuits/routes/allocation/status; validates timing-alarm causes before→Spacecraft Operations Team. Flight Dynamics Facility (Mistral): orbit/maneuver/visibility/pointing→planning. Mission Planning System: demands/constraints/Contact booking requests→plans. Command Validation Gateway: mandatory uplink barrier. Ground Network Manager (Juniper): antenna assignment/availability/conflicts/maintenance/staffing/site coordination; produces Antenna Deicing Notice; pins threatened critical paths before acquisition; latency investigation: carrier→routing/loss/queues/security→mission impact. Telemetry Ingest Service: real-time frames→framing/time-continuity checks/reception metadata→operations/engineering/processing; receives contact/data-flow indicators; produces Pass Replay Packet for engineering reconstruction. Orbit Determination Engine: tracking→orbit knowledge/Doppler Residual Report/state updates/visibility/maneuver/pointing predictions. Flight Dynamics Team: contact tracking/validated timestamps→Flight Dynamics Facility. Payload Processing Facility (Forgehouse): calibration/processing/distribution; Primary Processing Cluster nominal, archive transfers contact-rate-limited; Backup Processing Cluster controlled failover/lower preference/firewall-return-path testing. Product Quality Service: predissemination checks. Long Term Archive: authoritative data/products/records/traceability. User Services Portal: search/order/status/support. North S-Band Antenna/South S-Band Antenna: primary/alternate command/low-rate telemetry→Mission Control Center/protected routers. Kiruna X-Band Antenna/Svalbard X-Band Antenna: geometry/volume-justified high-rate→Payload Processing Facility/dual outage-tolerant paths. Spacecraft Operations Team: console monitoring mode/power/thermal/attitude/counters/storage/faults; displays emphasize deviations. Console lead declares status/authorizes commands/pauses unexpected configuration; telemetry engineer checks reception/loss/latency/continuity/command confidence; spacecraft systems engineer checks flight-rule compliance/anomaly context. Contact-close reconstruction combines commands/telemetry timing/station status/operator logs; assesses objectives/off-timeline events/analysis. Payload Calibration Team: calibration/quality. Cybersecurity Desk: Security Exception Ticket→temporary baseline deviations. Local station teams:

New part:
S093: The Mission Control Center coordinates with the Payload Processing Facility when instrument mode changes, data downlink priorities, or reception gaps could affect downstream processing.
S094: The Payload Calibration Team sends the Calibration Patch Bundle after calibration analysis identifies an approved update for payload processing behavior.
S095: Subsystem specialists are not expected to staff every live contact, but they must be reachable during planned critical activities and whenever a console operator declares an off-nominal condition.
S096: Escalation from the Mission Control Center begins with the console lead, moves to the responsible discipline lead, and then reaches mission management when the condition threatens spacecraft safety, contact continuity, or recovery schedule.
S097: The Spacecraft Operations Team and Flight Dynamics Team coordinate closely before orbit-control activities so that command timing, attitude constraints, tracking expectations, and post-burn assessment steps remain consistent.
S098: When telemetry indicates a possible onboard fault, operators preserve the command state, avoid discretionary commanding, and request specialist review before changing spacecraft configuration.
S099: The Mission Planning System receives operational constraints from mission control after anomalies, station outages, or spacecraft configuration changes require adjustment of future contacts or payload activities.
S100: At the end of each shift, the Mission Control Center records unresolved actions, open engineering questions, and expected specialist responses so that the next operations crew can maintain continuity without relying on informal handover.
S101: Mission planning begins when observation requests arrive through the User Services Portal or from internal operations channels at the Mission Control Center.
S102: The Mission Planning System, also called Cedar in this section, is the authoritative tool for assembling candidate observation timelines and associated ground contact activities.
S103: Each request is checked for requester authority, target definition, time sensitivity, acquisition mode, expected data volume, and any handling restrictions before it is admitted to the planning pool.
S104: The User Services Portal records the request state so that external users can distinguish accepted requests from those still awaiting technical review.
S105: The Spacecraft Operations Team reviews late operational requests when they affect spacecraft attitude, thermal margin, stored command capacity, or contact preparation.
S106: The Flight Dynamics Facility provides orbit predictions and visibility assumptions that the planning cycle uses to determine feasible imaging windows and ground contacts.
S107: The Mission Planning System combines request priority, instrument availability, contact opportunities, onboard storage margin, and downlink capacity into a draft activity schedule.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
